question: Can fixed inverse-retention scaling repair native half deletion, as predicted by distributed averaging?
inputs: All160 original task endpoints with source train/evaluation labels plus32 reused natural evaluation documents; no new holdout exposure.
theory: For uniformly retained n=N/2 channels c_i, unbiased estimate 2 sum_kept c_i has expected squared error (N sum_i ||c_i||²-||sum_i c_i||²)/(N-1). Bias remains once. Expectation is over masks, not a guarantee for these two complementary masks.
predictions: Aligned duplicate contributions admit near-exact compensation; orthogonal private contributions do not; large cancelling components can amplify error. Output repair also depends on downstream readers. One scalar correction tests a sufficient signature, not all possible redundancy.
selection: Frozen existing masks; no fitted scale, ranking, mask search, or threshold selected after outcomes.
limits: Context/task data familiar; paired masks are dependent. Even successful repair is not proof of identical semantic subfunctions, causal compensation by downstream layers, or an optimal pruning scheme.
stopping: Complete fixed comparison and audit; use results to refine the mechanism profile. No scale/mask sweep. Featurizer group-gate assay remains pending; native substitution is the priority under expanded objective.
